def: Relating to peroxisomes, organelles that oxidize very long-chain fatty acids and break down hydrogen peroxide. Defects cause Zellweger syndrome and adrenoleukodystrophy.
The white outer coats of the eyes. Blue sclerae occur in osteogenesis imperfecta, where thin collagen shows the underlying choroid.
Relating to the eyelids. The palpebral fissure is the opening between the eyelids, which is short in fetal alcohol syndrome and slanted upward in Down syndrome.
A small dip in the arterial pressure waveform caused by aortic valve closure and brief backflow. Marks the end of systole.
Ability of cardiac pacemaker cells to spontaneously depolarize and fire without outside stimulation. Greatest in the sinoatrial node.
The rate of myocardial relaxation. Positive lusitropy, such as from beta-1 stimulation, speeds calcium reuptake into the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Monoclonal antibody blocking the IL-6 receptor. Used for rheumatoid arthritis, giant cell arteritis and cytokine release syndrome.
Spiral septum dividing the truncus arteriosus into the aorta and pulmonary trunk. Neural crest cells form it; failure causes transposition of great vessels and truncus arteriosus.
Drugs that dilate veins, reducing preload and venous return. Nitroglycerin is the classic example.
Below the AV node, in the His-Purkinje system. Infranodal blocks are more dangerous and more likely to progress to complete heart block.
Coronary pattern in which the posterior descending artery arises from both the right and left coronary arteries, which occurs in a minority of people.
Monoclonal antibody inhibiting PCSK9, increasing LDL receptor recycling and lowering LDL cholesterol. Alirocumab is similar.
Lung pressure-volume curves differing on inflation and deflation, because more pressure is needed to open collapsed alveoli than keep them open.
Hemoglobin without bound oxygen, giving blood a bluish color. Pulse oximetry uses its different light absorption to measure saturation.
Binding of one oxygen molecule to hemoglobin increasing the affinity of the remaining sites, producing the sigmoidal oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve.
Relating to the fusion of a phagosome with a lysosome. In silicosis, macrophages that engulf silica rupture their phagolysosomes, causing inflammation and fibrosis.
Nuclear shrinkage with dense, dark chromatin, a feature of irreversible cell injury and cell death.
Having high blood chloride. Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis has a normal anion gap, from bicarbonate loss in diarrhea or renal tubular acidosis.
Excess amino acids in the urine from impaired renal reabsorption. Seen in Fanconi syndrome, cystinuria and Hartnup disease.
Liver enzyme phosphorylating fructose to fructose-1-phosphate. Deficiency causes benign essential fructosuria.
A clot that has broken off from where it formed and travels in the bloodstream to block a distant vessel.
5-lipoxygenase inhibitor that blocks leukotriene synthesis. Used in asthma; can cause hepatotoxicity.
Nephrons with glomeruli near the corticomedullary border and long loops of Henle that create the medullary concentration gradient.
Boundary between the renal cortex and medulla. Juxtamedullary glomeruli lie here.
Third embryonic kidney, which forms the permanent kidney. The ureteric bud forms the collecting system; the metanephric mesenchyme forms nephrons.
Having low urine output (under 400 mL/day). Seen in acute kidney injury.
Having crescents in Bowman space, from proliferation of parietal epithelial cells and macrophages. Seen in rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis.
Pus collection in the fat around the kidney, a complication of pyelonephritis. Presents with persistent fever despite antibiotics.
Sepsis originating from a urinary tract infection, often pyelonephritis or obstruction, requiring urgent treatment.
Having a normal serum calcium level. Most calcium oxalate stone formers have normal serum calcium and high urinary calcium.
Damaging the inner ear, causing hearing loss or imbalance. Examples include aminoglycosides, loop diuretics (especially ethacrynic acid) and cisplatin.
Intermediate in ketone body and cholesterol synthesis, made from two acetyl-CoA molecules. HMG-CoA synthase converts it to HMG-CoA.
Lysosomal enzyme that degrades heparan and dermatan sulfate. Deficiency causes Hurler syndrome.
Softening and ulceration of the cornea from severe vitamin A deficiency, often following xerophthalmia and Bitot spots.
Cracking and scaling at the lip corners and lips. Seen in riboflavin, iron and other vitamin deficiencies.
White cells with multilobed nuclei, mainly neutrophils. Hypersegmented ones (over 5 lobes) suggest B12 or folate deficiency.
Active form of vitamin B12 serving as cofactor for methionine synthase. Converts homocysteine to methionine.
Abnormally slow breathing rate. Seen in opioid overdose and in cholinergic toxicity.
Paralysis of the ciliary muscle, causing loss of accommodation and blurred near vision. Caused by antimuscarinics such as atropine.
Presence of abnormally large red blood cells (MCV above 100 fL). Seen in B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol use, liver disease and hypothyroidism.
Red cells with a bite taken out of the margin, seen in G6PD deficiency after Heinz bodies are removed by splenic macrophages.
